jobs.title: Model Evaluation Lead
jobs.description:
**Dyna Robotics** builds general-purpose robots powered by a proprietary embodied AI foundation model with top-in-industry generalization and real-world performance. Already deployed with customers across multiple industries, our robots do commercial-grade work in the physical world. Our team comes from Google DeepMind, Meta, and Cruise, and we're backed by CRV, First Round, and other leading investors.

**The Role**
============

Dyna Robotics is building general-purpose robots that perform useful work in real-world environments. We’re looking for a Model Evaluation Lead to lead the team responsible for understanding how our robot policies perform and whether new model versions deliver meaningful improvements.

You’ll manage and develop the evaluation team, own evaluation planning and execution, and work closely with researchers to define what we test, how we measure it, and what we learn. This is a hands-on leadership role combining people management, experimental rigor, and technical judgment. Your work will help researchers understand model behavior, prioritize improvements, and assess readiness for deployment.

**What You'll Do**
==================

* **Lead and develop the evaluation team.** Manage the team’s priorities, performance, and growth. Establish clear ownership, provide regular coaching and feedback, and build onboarding and training practices that help team members execute evaluations and investigate issues independently.
* **Work closely with researchers.** Translate research questions into evaluation plans with clear hypotheses, success criteria, and deliverables. Partner with researchers to compare model checkpoints, assess new capabilities, and balance recurring evaluations with urgent experiments and available robot capacity.
* **Design meaningful evaluations.** Develop task definitions, scoring rubrics, and test scenarios that reflect real operating conditions. Measure task success, output quality, cycle time, human interventions, and recovery behavior. Choose appropriate trial counts and account for variability when interpreting results.
* **Make results repeatable and trustworthy.** Standardize setup, resets, scoring, and intervention rules. Ensure results are traceable to model versions, robot configurations, test conditions, logs, and videos. Coordinate with hardware and operations partners to resolve issues that affect evaluation quality.
* **Turn failures into actionable findings.** Review robot behavior, logs, and video with the team and researchers. Distinguish model failures from hardware, software, setup, or execution issues. Identify recurring failure patterns and recommend focused investigations, additional data collection, or annotation improvements.
* **Own regression coverage and reporting.** Maintain consistent benchmarks and held-out test scenarios across tasks and conditions. Identify regressions, track progress across model versions, and communicate what improved, what remains unreliable, and where evidence is still limited. Provide clear recommendations that inform deployment decisions.
* **Improve evaluation tools and workflows.** Use data analysis and lightweight scripting to improve reporting and reduce manual work. Partner with engineering on evaluation tooling, automation, and dashboards. Shorten the time from a new checkpoint to useful findings while preserving the quality of the evidence.

**What You'll Bring**
=====================

* Experience in robotics, machine learning, applied research, or model evaluation, with direct ownership of evaluation design and analysis.
* Demonstrated experience managing and developing a technical team, including setting priorities, giving feedback, and building effective working practices.
* Strong experimental judgment: you can define success, control relevant variables, identify gaps in test coverage, and assess whether an apparent improvement is meaningful.
* Technical fluency to work directly with researchers on model checkpoints, generalization, data quality, and experimental tradeoffs.
* Comfort using Python or similar tools to analyze results, inspect logs, and improve evaluation workflows.
* Clear communication and strong ownership. You can turn an ambiguous request into an executable plan, surface problems early, and explain findings to both research and operations teams.

**Bonus Points For**
====================

* Evaluating robot manipulation policies, embodied AI, autonomous systems, or other machine learning systems operating in the physical world.
* Building regression suites, benchmark datasets, failure taxonomies, or evaluation tools, and connecting findings to model development or deployment readiness.

*At* ***Dyna Robotics****, we build technology for the real world, which requires a team as diverse as the environments our robots inhabit. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to technical rigor and mutual respect.*

***Don’t let a checklist stop you.*** *Data shows that underrepresented groups often only apply if they meet 100% of the criteria. We value problem-solving and grit over keyword matching. If you’re passionate about robotics, no matter your discipline, we want to hear from you, even if you don't check every box.*

Compensation Range: $140K - $160K

jobs.title: AI Engineer, Medical Vision Language Models
jobs.description:
Lumexa Imaging is one of the country's largest providers of outpatient medical imaging. With over 5,000 team members and more than 185 outpatient imaging centers across 13 states, our team conducts more than 4 million outpatient studies annually. We are the partner of choice for health systems and radiologists, delivering best-in-class clinical excellence, operations, and state-of-the-art technology across our platform.
  
  
Lumexa Imaging is hiring an early-career AI Engineer to help build, adapt, and deploy vision language models (VLMs) and imaging foundation models for clinical radiology. You will work hands-on using agentic coding tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex) to transition ideas from radiologists into validated, deployed models. This is a build-focused role centered on model development and deployment.
  
  
Initial priorities include building clinical LLM pipelines (prior report summarization, scanned document summarization, and relevant prior selection) on infrastructure shared with our VLM work.
  
  
**Why this role is a rare opportunity:** You will have access to a large, growing repository of clinical imaging and reporting data. A central part of this job is leveraging this real-world, domain-specific data, consistent with applicable privacy, security, and governance requirements, to develop, adapt, and evaluate AI models beyond what is possible using public data alone.
  
  
You will work closely with the Chief Clinical AI Officer, the Clinical Applications team, and Infrastructure and Information Security.
  
  
**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**  

* VLM Development and Adaptation: Fine-tune and adapt open VLMs (e.g., Qwen-VL, LLaVA-Med, MedGemma, InternVL) and imaging foundation models for report drafting, impression generation, finding detection, and prior comparison. Apply parameter-efficient methods (LoRA, QLoRA) and full fine-tuning under senior guidance.
* Vision Encoders and Representation Learning: Work with vision encoders, contrastive image-text models (CLIP, SigLIP), and self-supervised approaches (JEPA). Build and maintain embedding pipelines for retrieval, cohort discovery, case similarity search, and drift detection
* Data Curation: Curate and version datasets from our internal PACS and reporting systems, including DICOM header, burned-in pixel, and paired-report de-identification
* Agentic Engineering: Use Claude Code and OpenAI Codex daily to build, test, and maintain code. Maintain project context (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md), and help build and run MCP servers for internal system access
* Deployment and MLOps: Deploy models via containerized inference and GPU serving (vLLM, Triton), support CI/CD pipelines, and monitor production models for drift and performance
* Evaluation: Build automated evaluation harnesses for clinical accuracy, negation, laterality, and hallucination scoring against radiologist ground truth
* Workflow Automation: Build agentic and LLM driven tools for operational workflows, such as converting unstructured requests into RIS scheduling actions and supporting intelligent operations dashboards

**Required Qualifications:**  

* Hands-on experience fine-tuning transformer models in PyTorch (vision, multimodal, or language) using Hugging Face, MONAI, or similar (via internships, research, open-source work, or projects)
* Working knowledge of embeddings and vector search
* Experience with open VLMs such as Qwen-VL or LLaVA
* Daily use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex)
* Familiarity with Docker and GPU-based model serving
* Comfort working with real-world data and a reproducible approach to experiments

**Preferred Qualifications:**  

* Hands-on experience with vision encoders and contrastive models (CLIP, SigLIP, JEPA)
* Exposure to medical VLMs, imaging foundation models, or self-supervised methods (DINOv2, MAE)
* Experience building MCP servers in Python or TypeScript
* Familiarity with medical imaging formats (DICOM, HL7, FHIR) and HIPAA/PHI handling
* Awareness of MLOps tooling (MLflow, Weights & Biases, model registries)
* Awareness of FDA considerations for clinical AI (510(k), PCCP)

**Education/Licensing/Certification:**  
Degree in Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
  
  
**Experience (years and type):**  
Experience 0 to 3 years (internships, research, or projects count)
  
**Travel Required (% of time):** Minimal, up to 10%
  
**Physical Requirements & Work Environment:** Standard remote office work
  
  
Lumexa Imaging provides a competitive compensation program to attract, retain, and motivate a high-performance workforce.
  
  
Lumexa Imaging is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, AI Security
jobs.description:
**About Tolmo**
---------------

Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. The old playbook of quarterly pentests and endless alert queues breaks at this speed.

We're building a new security playbook. Tolmo runs a fleet of AI security agents that reason over a live graph of your entire production system (code, CI, cloud, and telemetry) and continuously attack a faithful copy of it like a real adversary. Every finding arrives validated, with its blast radius and a remediation plan that lands in your workflow, ready for a coding agent to fix. Hours to integrate, days to your first validated finding.

We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.

**The role**
------------

Our product is only as good as our agents' judgment. As a Research Engineer on AI Security, you make that judgment better and measurably so: how our agents plan, reason over a graph of a customer's production system, decide what is worth testing, and know when a finding is real.

This sits between research and engineering. In one week you might design an eval that catches a new class of false positive, change how an agent plans a multi-step investigation, compare models on a hard benchmark, and harden the agents themselves against prompt injection from the systems they inspect. You'll work directly with the founders, our engineers, and the security leads who run pentests with our agents, and your work ships to production.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* **Agent reasoning:** improve how our agents plan, use tools, and reason over a live graph of code, cloud, and telemetry, so they reach real findings faster and with fewer dead ends.
* **Evaluation:** build the evals, benchmarks, and graders that tell us whether an agent actually got better, and make them part of how every change ships.
* **Model selection and tuning:** compare models, prompts, and agent designs on cost, latency, and quality, and turn the results into production decisions.
* **Model and agent security:** defend our agents against prompt injection, data exfiltration, and manipulation by the very systems they test, and research the security of LLM-based applications our customers build.
* **Reliability at scale:** make long-running agents dependable across thousands of runs: verification, self-checks, and sensible stopping.
* **Learning from the field:** study agent runs from customer engagements, find where reasoning broke, and turn each failure into an eval and a fix.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* Hands-on experience building, evaluating, or improving LLM-based agents or systems in production.
* A rigorous, empirical approach: you design experiments, distrust single anecdotes, and let the evals decide.
* Strong engineering skills: you write production-quality code (Python, TypeScript, or Go) and build tools other people rely on.
* A working understanding of security, or a strong drive to learn it fast: how real systems are attacked and how findings are validated.
* Familiarity with LLM security risks such as prompt injection, jailbreaks, and tool misuse.
* You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and have opinions about what makes them reliable.

**Nice to have**
----------------

* Research background in machine learning, AI safety, or security: publications, open-source work, or talks.
* Offensive security experience: penetration testing, red teaming, bug bounty, or CTFs.
* Experience with reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, or synthetic data generation for agents.
* Experience with graph data models or reasoning over structured data.
* Prior early-stage startup experience.

**Compensation & benefits**
---------------------------

* **Competitive salary**, depending on level and experience.
* **Early-stage equity:** you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.
* Based in San Francisco; we work in person.

*Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.*

jobs.title: Senior Research Engineer, Robotics
jobs.description:
**About Tutor**

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**The Role**

Tutor's research team pushes the frontier of robot capability across the full stack. Researchers have access to 100+ robots for data collection and evaluation, a massive network of teleoperators, scaled hardware and manufacturing infrastructure, and the ability to collect real world data at enormous scale. Our work covers the complete lifecycle of real-world data generation and model training from initial behavior cloning to post-training with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. And researchers and research engineers work closely with applied engineers to develop novel techniques into robot products that can be deployed at scale.

As a research engineer on robotics, you'll turn research ideas into experiments that run on real robots, and make the results trustworthy.

### **What you'll work on**

* Build and run policy experiments on DF1, from task setup and data collection through rollouts and analysis.
* Own evaluation: task suites, success metrics, and tooling that make results comparable across robots, operators, and model versions.
* Build the robot-side software that runs policies: inference, control interfaces, safety limits, and logging.
* Improve the intervention loop, so teleoperators can step in when a policy fails and that data flows back into training.
* Debug failures that cross perception, control, hardware, and model behavior.
* Work with research scientists on what to try next, and with applied engineers on what's ready to deploy.

### **Requirements**

* Strong Python, and maintainable, tested code that runs on real hardware.
* Hands-on experience running learned policies or other autonomy on physical robots.
* Experience designing experiments and judging whether a result is real.
* Comfort debugging across Linux, networking, sensors, and robot control.

### **Nice to haves**

* Robot arms and manipulation; ROS or a similar framework.
* PyTorch and GPU inference.
* Teleoperation or VR systems.
* C++.

### **Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

### **Benefits**

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

new_jobs.title: AI Engineer, Medical Vision Language Models
new_jobs.description:
Lumexa Imaging is one of the country's largest providers of outpatient medical imaging. With over 5,000 team members and more than 185 outpatient imaging centers across 13 states, our team conducts more than 4 million outpatient studies annually. We are the partner of choice for health systems and radiologists, delivering best-in-class clinical excellence, operations, and state-of-the-art technology across our platform.
  
  
Lumexa Imaging is hiring an early-career AI Engineer to help build, adapt, and deploy vision language models (VLMs) and imaging foundation models for clinical radiology. You will work hands-on using agentic coding tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex) to transition ideas from radiologists into validated, deployed models. This is a build-focused role centered on model development and deployment.
  
  
Initial priorities include building clinical LLM pipelines (prior report summarization, scanned document summarization, and relevant prior selection) on infrastructure shared with our VLM work.
  
  
**Why this role is a rare opportunity:** You will have access to a large, growing repository of clinical imaging and reporting data. A central part of this job is leveraging this real-world, domain-specific data, consistent with applicable privacy, security, and governance requirements, to develop, adapt, and evaluate AI models beyond what is possible using public data alone.
  
  
You will work closely with the Chief Clinical AI Officer, the Clinical Applications team, and Infrastructure and Information Security.
  
  
**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**  

* VLM Development and Adaptation: Fine-tune and adapt open VLMs (e.g., Qwen-VL, LLaVA-Med, MedGemma, InternVL) and imaging foundation models for report drafting, impression generation, finding detection, and prior comparison. Apply parameter-efficient methods (LoRA, QLoRA) and full fine-tuning under senior guidance.
* Vision Encoders and Representation Learning: Work with vision encoders, contrastive image-text models (CLIP, SigLIP), and self-supervised approaches (JEPA). Build and maintain embedding pipelines for retrieval, cohort discovery, case similarity search, and drift detection
* Data Curation: Curate and version datasets from our internal PACS and reporting systems, including DICOM header, burned-in pixel, and paired-report de-identification
* Agentic Engineering: Use Claude Code and OpenAI Codex daily to build, test, and maintain code. Maintain project context (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md), and help build and run MCP servers for internal system access
* Deployment and MLOps: Deploy models via containerized inference and GPU serving (vLLM, Triton), support CI/CD pipelines, and monitor production models for drift and performance
* Evaluation: Build automated evaluation harnesses for clinical accuracy, negation, laterality, and hallucination scoring against radiologist ground truth
* Workflow Automation: Build agentic and LLM driven tools for operational workflows, such as converting unstructured requests into RIS scheduling actions and supporting intelligent operations dashboards

**Required Qualifications:**  

* Hands-on experience fine-tuning transformer models in PyTorch (vision, multimodal, or language) using Hugging Face, MONAI, or similar (via internships, research, open-source work, or projects)
* Working knowledge of embeddings and vector search
* Experience with open VLMs such as Qwen-VL or LLaVA
* Daily use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex)
* Familiarity with Docker and GPU-based model serving
* Comfort working with real-world data and a reproducible approach to experiments

**Preferred Qualifications:**  

* Hands-on experience with vision encoders and contrastive models (CLIP, SigLIP, JEPA)
* Exposure to medical VLMs, imaging foundation models, or self-supervised methods (DINOv2, MAE)
* Experience building MCP servers in Python or TypeScript
* Familiarity with medical imaging formats (DICOM, HL7, FHIR) and HIPAA/PHI handling
* Awareness of MLOps tooling (MLflow, Weights & Biases, model registries)
* Awareness of FDA considerations for clinical AI (510(k), PCCP)

**Education/Licensing/Certification:**  
Degree in Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
  
  
**Experience (years and type):**  
Experience 0 to 3 years (internships, research, or projects count)
  
**Travel Required (% of time):** Minimal, up to 10%
  
**Physical Requirements & Work Environment:** Standard remote office work

Lumexa Imaging is an equal opportunity employer.

new_jobs.title: Research Engineer, AI Security
new_jobs.description:
**About Tolmo**
---------------

Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. The old playbook of quarterly pentests and endless alert queues breaks at this speed.

We're building a new security playbook. Tolmo runs a fleet of AI security agents that reason over a live graph of your entire production system (code, CI, cloud, and telemetry) and continuously attack a faithful copy of it like a real adversary. Every finding arrives validated, with its blast radius and a remediation plan that lands in your workflow, ready for a coding agent to fix. Hours to integrate, days to your first validated finding.

We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.

**The role**
------------

Our product is only as good as our agents' judgment. As a Research Engineer on AI Security, you make that judgment better and measurably so: how our agents plan, reason over a graph of a customer's production system, decide what is worth testing, and know when a finding is real.

This sits between research and engineering. In one week you might design an eval that catches a new class of false positive, change how an agent plans a multi-step investigation, compare models on a hard benchmark, and harden the agents themselves against prompt injection from the systems they inspect. You'll work directly with the founders, our engineers, and the security leads who run pentests with our agents, and your work ships to production.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* **Agent reasoning:** improve how our agents plan, use tools, and reason over a live graph of code, cloud, and telemetry, so they reach real findings faster and with fewer dead ends.
* **Evaluation:** build the evals, benchmarks, and graders that tell us whether an agent actually got better, and make them part of how every change ships.
* **Model selection and tuning:** compare models, prompts, and agent designs on cost, latency, and quality, and turn the results into production decisions.
* **Model and agent security:** defend our agents against prompt injection, data exfiltration, and manipulation by the very systems they test, and research the security of LLM-based applications our customers build.
* **Reliability at scale:** make long-running agents dependable across thousands of runs: verification, self-checks, and sensible stopping.
* **Learning from the field:** study agent runs from customer engagements, find where reasoning broke, and turn each failure into an eval and a fix.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* Hands-on experience building, evaluating, or improving LLM-based agents or systems in production.
* A rigorous, empirical approach: you design experiments, distrust single anecdotes, and let the evals decide.
* Strong engineering skills: you write production-quality code (Python, TypeScript, or Go) and build tools other people rely on.
* A working understanding of security, or a strong drive to learn it fast: how real systems are attacked and how findings are validated.
* Familiarity with LLM security risks such as prompt injection, jailbreaks, and tool misuse.
* You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and have opinions about what makes them reliable.

**Nice to have**
----------------

* Research background in machine learning, AI safety, or security: publications, open-source work, or talks.
* Offensive security experience: penetration testing, red teaming, bug bounty, or CTFs.
* Experience with reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, or synthetic data generation for agents.
* Experience with graph data models or reasoning over structured data.
* Prior early-stage startup experience.

**Compensation & benefits**
---------------------------

* **Competitive salary**, depending on level and experience.
* **Early-stage equity:** you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.
* Based in San Francisco; we work in person.

*Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.*
